clue.text: Words of old chief end when son interrupts

parts.note: arch- as a word means chief or principal, as in arch-enemy

indicators.note: the son interrupts the end, so its letter breaks into the middle of that word

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A tribal chief's line ends abruptly when his son butts in.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaism is an antiquated expression, a word or phrase from an earlier period of the language.

clue.text: Various notes produced by bow

parts.note: six separate musical notes from the scale, each a single letter from A to G
six separate musical notes from the scale, each a single letter from A to G
six separate musical notes from the scale, each a single letter from A to G
six separate musical notes from the scale, each a single letter from A to G
six separate musical notes from the scale, each a single letter from A to G
six separate musical notes from the scale, each a single letter from A to G

explanation.surface: A violin bow produces a run of different notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' looks like the violinist's tool; it is the verb, to bow to or give way.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede is to agree or give way, as one bows to another's wishes.

clue.text: Celebrate driving with old passenger?

indicators.note: the old one rides as a passenger inside the car use

parts.note: car use, driving a car

explanation.surface: Celebrating by driving around with an elderly passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink and make merry, to celebrate noisily.

clue.text: Horrify a friend, abandoning northern US mining area

parts.note: to appal is to horrify

indicators.note: the friend abandons the northern letter, losing it

parts.note: china is rhyming slang, china plate for mate

explanation.surface: Disgusting a pal by leaving the north for a US coalfield.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate), and losing N leaves CHIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Appalachia is the US mountain region famous for coal mining.

clue.text: Square, earthed switch?

definitions.meaning: a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person
a switch is a thin stick; earthed, it is planted in the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A stick-in-the-mud is an unadventurous conformist, a square; literally a stick in the soil.

clue.text: Response to joke about new Conservative leader

indicators.note: the laughter goes round about the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: laughter written out as ho-ho
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British political party

explanation.surface: Someone laughs at a quip about the newly elected Tory leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Honcho is American slang, from Japanese, for the boss or person in charge.

clue.text: Cereal's temperature lowest here? Anything but!

definitions.text: Cereal's temperature lowest here? Anything but!

indicators.note: in this down entry the letter for temperature should sit lowest, at the bottom, but it is moved anywhere else

parts.note: oats are a cereal

explanation.surface: Is this where grain is kept coolest? Quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry OATS has T at the bottom; moving it up gives the kiln, where heat is highest, not lowest.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, a very hot place.

clue.text: Country's agents to hold up groups of soldiers

indicators.note: the agents hold the soldiers inside

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency, its agents

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British reserve force, and OR other ranks
TA is the Territorial Army, the British reserve force, and OR other ranks

explanation.surface: Agents in a country holding up army units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the soldiers to ROAT and 'to hold' puts that inside. The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve; other ranks are soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a country in the Balkans.

clue.text: This is not OK, run together online

parts.note: split as on line: on means over (about), and a line is a rule
split as on line: on means over (about), and a line is a rule

explanation.surface: An instruction that something is wrong, posted together on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run together' says ON LINE is written as the single word 'online', which disguises it as the internet sense. 'This is not OK' is an example of the act: a superior's ruling that a decision is rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrule is to reject a decision, in effect declaring it not acceptable.

clue.text: Tails in exotic menu appear to come from dog

indicators.note: the tails of the three words that follow are their final letters

explanation.surface: Endings on a foreign menu seem to suggest the meat is canine.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a mongrel or worthless dog, a standard synonym.

clue.text: Minimal range of camping equipment

parts.note: a range is a kitchen cooker; the smallest cooker of all is the little paraffin burner packed for a camping trip

explanation.surface: A small selection of tents and gear on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like an assortment of goods, but it is the old-fashioned kitchen cooking range, shrunk to camp size.
explanation.definitionFit: A Primus is the brand-name portable paraffin cooker long used by campers, a minimal cooking range.

clue.text: Drunk as a rule, men visit this local in Greenwich?

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: Men regularly drop into this pub in Greenwich after drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like a pub; it is local time, the clock kept at Greenwich. 'Drunk' rearranges A RULE MEN VISIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal time is the world standard based on the mean solar time at Greenwich, its local time.

clue.text: Type of fabric, older kind, is regularly unreliable?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Type of fabric, older kind, is regularly unreliable?' for DOUBLE KNIT: LEKNI (alternate letters of 'older kind, is') in DOUBT, but 'unreliable' does two jobs, as DOUBT and as the 'in' container signal (in doubt).
annotationWithheld.clue: Type of fabric, older kind, is regularly unreliable?

clue.text: Activity between "sit around" and "run"?

indicators.note: the word sit is turned around, its letters rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what falls between sitting and running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges STI. 'Activity' covers the whole idea: a stir is the bustle between sitting still and running off.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a commotion or bustle of activity, as in causing a stir.

clue.text: Unloved doctor who's possibly rejected holy communion

parts.note: Doctor Fell of the rhyme 'I do not love thee, Dr Fell'

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: the word who's, read as letters

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so read backwards

parts.note: pi is slang for pious or holy

explanation.surface: A disliked Doctor Who fan possibly refused holy communion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges WHOS into OWSH; 'rejected' turns PI to IP. 'Doctor who' looks like the TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellowship means communion, a sharing of common interests or spirit.

clue.text: One churchman or another holding firm

indicators.note: the dean holds the firm, keeping it inside

parts.note: another churchman, a dean, head of a cathedral chapter
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Two clergymen, one of them clutching a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister ranking below a priest, so one kind of churchman.

clue.text: Examine recorded confession of one shouting?

indicators.note: recorded suggests sound played back, so the words are heard rather than written

parts.note: someone shouting admits 'I bawl'

explanation.surface: A taped admission from someone who yells under interrogation.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball something is to look at it closely, to scrutinise or inspect it.

clue.text: During computer game, scrape up cash at last for spirits

indicators.note: these letters go inside the computer game

parts.note: a sim is a simulation computer game

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read backwards

parts.note: to pare is to scrape or shave

indicators.note: the last letter of the word cash

explanation.surface: Scraping up money to play a video game for strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphim are angels of the highest order, heavenly spirits.

clue.text: Supply help, mostly, with sign language

indicators.note: supply read as supple, bendy, so the letters are flexed into a new order
most of the word help, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: Providing support to the deaf by signing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops a letter to give HEL; 'Supply' (as in suppl-y, in a supple way) rearranges the pool. 'Sign language' looks like one phrase, but it splits.
explanation.definitionFit: English is the language of England and much of the world.

clue.text: Darker glasses required if meeting ministers, especially religious leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters

parts.words: glasses required if meeting ministers, especially religious

explanation.surface: Advice to wear sunglasses when meeting clerics.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimmer means gloomier or bleaker, darker in mood.

clue.text: Hack secures page headline …

indicators.note: the slash secures the page by holding it inside

parts.note: to hack is to slash or cut roughly

explanation.surface: A journalist locks in a front-page headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' wants to be a journalist; it is the verb, to slash.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a big front-page story or headline, in newspaper jargon.

clue.text: Cut off as sea is rising, engulfing cape

indicators.note: the reversed letters engulf the cape
in a down entry, rising means read upwards

parts.note: the Ross Sea in Antarctica

explanation.surface: Cut off as the tide rises and swallows a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reads the sea and 'is' upwards as SISSOR, which 'engulfing' wraps round the cape. The Ross Sea lies off Antarctica.
explanation.definitionFit: To scissor is to cut with scissors, so cut off.

clue.text: Taking wine during imposition of penalty shows lack of respect

indicators.note: the wine goes during the levy, inside it

parts.note: a levy is an imposition, a charge
It is Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Drinking during the penalty shows disrespect.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity is frivolity, a lack of seriousness or respect.

clue.text: … in the centre, in morning papers

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means morning
ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: Continuing the headline: right in the middle of the morning newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid means in the middle of or surrounded by, a preposition of position.

clue.text: Everyone's in the swim, swimming the butterfly

indicators.note: everyone is placed inside the scrambled letters
swimming suggests letters moving about, rearranged

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: Everybody is in the pool, doing butterfly stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges the letters around a gap filled by 'in'. 'Butterfly' looks like the swimming stroke; it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The small white is a common European butterfly, a cabbage pest.

clue.text: Oscar follower's nonsense on opening of awards

parts.note: pap is worthless nonsense

indicators.note: the first letter of awards

explanation.surface: A film critic dismisses the Oscar ceremony as tripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' looks like the film award; in the NATO alphabet Papa comes after Oscar.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for P follows the one for O.

clue.text: Amateur press's simple fare?

parts.note: a ham is an amateur, especially an amateur radio operator or poor actor
to sandwich is to press between two things

explanation.surface: An amateur printing press producing plain material.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham sandwich is a plain, everyday snack, simple food.

clue.text: Alpine runner's short fleece

indicators.note: the word is cut short, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to fleece is to skin, to cheat of money

explanation.surface: A mountain athlete wears a cropped fleece jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete, but a ski runs on snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a runner for gliding over snow, used in Alpine sport.

clue.text: Lots of farm girls return, deprived of equipment

indicators.note: what is left is read backwards
the girls lose the equipment from their letters

parts.note: dairymaids are girls working on a farm
aids are equipment, devices that help

explanation.surface: Many farm girls come back with no tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of' leaves DAIRYM, which 'return' turns round. 'Lots' looks like a verb in the surface, but it is a noun phrase meaning a great many.
explanation.definitionFit: Myriad means a countless number, lots.

clue.text: Social occasion but, contrarily, drinks not included

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, swallowing the other piece
contrarily means the word goes the wrong way, read backwards

parts.note: but and yet are synonyms as conjunctions
apart means separate, not included

explanation.surface: A party where, oddly enough, no drinks are provided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrarily' gives TEY, which 'drinks' (takes in) around APART. The clue reads like a teetotal party.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea party is an afternoon gathering, a type of social occasion.
